entries.title: Proverbs 13:6
segments: 6. A sentiment of frequent recurrence, that piety benefits and sin injures.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:7
segments: 7. In opposite ways men act hypocritically for gain of honor or wealth.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:8
segments: 8. Riches save some from punishment, while others suffer because they will not heed the rebuke of sloth, which makes and keeps them poor.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:9
segments:
9. light ... lamp--prosperity; the first, the greater, and it 
 
    rejoiceth--burns brightly, or continues, while the other, at best small, soon fails.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:10
segments: 10. The obstinacy which attends self-conceit, produces contention, which the well-advised, thus evincing modesty, avoid.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:11
segments:
11. by vanity--or, "nothingness," that is, which is vain or useless to the public (as card playing or similar vices). 
 
    gathereth ... labour--(Compare Margin), little by little, laboriously.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:12
segments:
12. desire cometh--is realized. 
 
    a tree of life--or, "cause of happiness."

entries.title: Proverbs 13:17
segments:
17. A wicked--or, "unfaithful" 
 
    messenger falleth into mischief--or, "by mischief," or "evil," and so his errand fails. Contrasted is the character of the faithful, whose faithfulness benefits others.

segments: 23. The laboring poor prosper more than those who injudiciously or wickedly strive, by fraud and violence, to supersede the necessity of lawful labor.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:25
segments: 25. The comparative temporal prosperity of the righteous and wicked, rather than contentment and discontent, is noted.
